svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A mass spectrometer measures the masses and abundances of isotopes."], [1, "The sample is vaporised and ionised."], [3, "Positive ions are accelerated by an electric field."], [5, "A magnetic field deflects them: lighter ions bend more."], [8, "The detector counts the ions of each mass."], [10.5, "The mass spectrum of chlorine: two isotopes, about 3 : 1."], [13, "Weighted mean: Ar(Cl) = 35.5."]]
svg.title: The mass spectrometer
svg.desc: A magnetic sector mass spectrometer: vaporisation, ionisation by electron bombardment, acceleration, deflection in a magnetic field with lighter ions bent more, and detection; the mass spectrum of chlorine and its relative atomic mass.
svg.text: Simplified magnetic-sector instrument; the whole tube is under vacuum.

g.data-info: The sample is turned into a gas.
High-energy electrons knock an electron off each atom: X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.
An electric field accelerates the positive ions to high speed.
A magnetic field bends their paths: lighter ions (lower m/z) are deflected more.
Ions hit the detector, which records how many of each m/z arrive.
Peak height shows relative abundance. Chlorine: ³⁵Cl 75.8%, ³⁷Cl 24.2%.

g.text: a weighted mean of the isotope masses
